utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander who was in the room and talked to the guards who had brought us from Bosanski Novi there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reply that you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That our throats should be cut because we were Ustashi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which of the two men said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because I was facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they took us and took us to a cell in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men that beat you, did you know either of them prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever met a person by the name of Tadic prior to this date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Met?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever met a person by the name of Tadic prior to this date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anyone by that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that what happened then? Where did you go then, after the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they took us to the cell in the barracks and there they beat us for the second time, other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are they that beat you, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I do not know -- soldiers too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same men that had beat you previously or was it different men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Different men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that? Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent one night there and then they took us to the camp at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay when you were taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Omarska did you recognise any of the guards that were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know anyone from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the white house at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you spent in the white house at Omarska were you ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five times a day at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come to know any of the men that beat you during the time that you were kept in the white house at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether I came to know one of the guards?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could only hear their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you remember any of the names that were used against some of the guards that had beaten you when you were in the camp at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want me to give you the names?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can remember them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was somebody called Kvocka, he was a Commander of the camp for a while, then he was replaced by Zeljko Meakic who also beat me personally; and from Prijedor came some guards, one of them was Zuga Nikica and there was another one with them, Pirvan, then another one called Brk, he was a personal driver for Zeljko Meakic, and a number of others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the camp was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. It must have been August or September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: August and September of what year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where did you go after you left Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you kept on Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until mid December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where did you go after you were in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left with the International Red Cross convoy and we went to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back for a moment to the time when you went to the Prijedor barracks where you were beaten by those two men, when you first heard the name "Tadic", what position were you standing in at that moment when you first heard the name "Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was facing the wall with three fingers against wall, and when I wanted to look at them, I saw two men come in and one of them hit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June of this year, June 14th June 1996, were you shown a book of photographs by Mr. Thomas Ackheim and Mr. Reid of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a booklet with photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look through each of those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the photographs there that you saw in the booklet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph that you recognised, who was that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that photograph was one of the two who beat us at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that photograph, the photograph of that person, prior to this time when were you shown the photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen the image of this person on television or any other media form prior to this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might I have this photo book marked for identification, please, No. 242? Might the photo book be shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of that, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We do not, your Honour. Your Honour may recollect there were submissions about this subject before our break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have an extra copy of 242 for the Defence to look at while the witness is looking at this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, we have seen the booklet and I made copies myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We gave a copy to the Defence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good, thank you. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Mr. Halvadzic, does that appear to be the book that you were shown by investigators Ackheim and Reid from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on one of the photographs in that book, on the back of one of the photographs in that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What photograph in number from the front of the book does it appear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are two figures here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. How many photographs into the book is it from the front of the book? Can you just count up the photographs from the front of the book?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All I want you to tell me is how many photographs in from the beginning of the book is that photograph that you have signed? Go to the front of the book, right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here the second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you were about to quote some numbers to us there appearing on the back of that photograph. Were those numbers on the photograph when you signed it, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was just blank, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, your Honour, we sustain the objection we already made though the matter is pending, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then I will assume that you have a running objection to the use ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- of this photo booklet in this procedure for the reasons you stated in your submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be overruled at this time. Exhibit 242 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you sure that the photograph that you have written your name on the back of was the person that beat you at the Prijedor barracks on that day, or one of the men that beat you at the Prijedor barracks on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Halvadzic, I can assume, can I not, that you live in a place at the moment where there are televisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can assume, can I not, that you live in a place where there are newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you aware that you were going to be a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they found me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they find you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in May of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a statement here signed by you on 4th May 1995. I will take that as being the approximate time that you were located to be a witness in this case, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will take it that the statement dated 4th May 1995 would have been about the time that you were approached to be a witness in this case, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was nearly three years after the events that have taken place in Prijedor barracks when you were first arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the meantime you had spent nearly three months in the camp of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Omarska you went to a camp called Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in Manjaca for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About six months or four months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Altogether in both camps?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three to four months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. From Manjaca you went to a place called Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date was it that you were released and able to leave the life of living in a camp either as a refugee or as a detainee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when I was released from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was around 15th December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend time as a refugee living in a camp outside Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was in Karlovac for a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a month you were in Karlovac and was that the last time that you lived in a camp? Did you take up life elsewhere living in ordinary accommodation after Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was still a refugee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you gave a statement three years after the events that took place in Prijedor barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are shown a photo book in June of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just over four years after the events that took place in Prijedor barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that this trial has been on television, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know but I did not watch it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that an honest answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you watched the news at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no time to watch the news.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen newspapers covering this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you walked around the streets or been in anyone's house when the television has been on and seen coverage of this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not watch any transmissions and my knowledge of [redacted] would not allow me to follow that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, but you can look at pictures, can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was forbidden to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that does not stop you looking at pictures, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an honest man. I am a sincere man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have an interest in this case because you knew you were going to be a witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No interest, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No interest. So you are telling us then that you have not seen any coverage in newspapers or on television concerning this trial and you are being honest about that, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Prijedor barracks and you were attacked by the man you say was called Tadic, were all the men military policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the room where they were, there were only military policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guard who attacked you called Tadic, was he dressed as a military policeman as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By being dressed as a military policeman, we mean wearing a white belt.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what military policemen wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have anything else with him, any other equipment, that a military policeman might have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a white baton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A white baton? You can remember seeing the white baton whereabouts on his person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I also remember him wearing -- having a knife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell me where the white baton was first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On his right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Attached to his belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, attached to his belt on the right-hand side. On the left side he had a knife. On the right side he had the baton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that we understand it, can you tell us how big the white baton was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About half a metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The knife that was on his person, was that also attached to the belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a bayonet, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of size was that knife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also about 40 centimetres -- maybe a little smaller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You describe being attacked by two men, was the second man, the other man, also a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two who brought us from Bosanski Novi were also military policemen from Bosanski Novi who had brought us to the Prijedor barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two guards who came in of whom you said one was called Tadic, was the other one a military policeman as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were both members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it seemed to be that you were in a place where the military police were working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the barracks and there were only Serbian soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but the group of men that you were amongst in this room appear to have all been military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the corridor in front of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group of men who were dealing with you appeared to be military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was sure. It did not "appear"; I was sure they were military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can assume that was their job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who beat us, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes -- no, to be military policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were reserve servicemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many people are called "Tadic" in the Prijedor region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know there is a village called Tadici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know there is a village called Babici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know there is a village called Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you have never met anyone by the name of Tadic before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this trial started did you watch any of the programmes on television about the arrest of a man called Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have only heard that a man named Tadic had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A friend of mine told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A friend. Why did your friend tell that you a man called Tadic had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me if I knew him, if I knew someone called Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As he thought you might be interested in these kinds of matters, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would seek out war criminals myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and that is why you would watch television programmes, even before this trial started, because you are interested in these matters, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only watch films on television, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not watch any news that comes on between the films?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no news between films.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about a film by a lady called Monika Gras?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You look at newspapers, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only newspaper I ever look at was [redacted] newspaper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So despite all that happened to you by being in Omarska, Manjaca, being arrested, you have not taken any interest in the news describing events upon those matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I do not believe in propaganda which is mostly lies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you have told in this court, is it not? You have told lies about not seeing any images on television or in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told lies about the name "Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone else's name mentioned in Prijedor barracks on that day that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only "Tadic" was called out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No other names of anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the other five or six?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the other five or six people who had dealings with you, no other names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not mentioned, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other names that you can remember relating to guards in Omarska other than the well-known ones of Zeljko Meakic, any other names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have said, Pirvan. I remember two brothers, twins, guards. They had curly hair. I do not remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you about names, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any names of guards in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, how many times a day were you beaten in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At least five times a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any names used then? Did guards refer to names amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember any of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have said, Pirvan, Duca, Zigic, Nikica, Brk, Krkan, Ckalja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are all of all the important people in Omarska, camps commanders and shift leaders, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all beat me in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the commanders beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Commander and the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Omarska at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it just happens that you can remember amongst all those events that happened to you the name of this one reservist military policeman being called out as "Tadic", is that what it comes to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard his name a couple of times in Omarska too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have made it up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann? Re-examined by MR. NIEMANN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Halvadzic, could you tell us about the circumstances where you heard the name Tadic mentioned in the camp at Omarska, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, with reference to our submissions that we had this morning in open court, we have not had a written judgment from the Court yet relating to hearsay, and I am very mindful of your Honours' remarks concerning veracity and other indicators as to whether hearsay, as far as your Honour is concerned, should be used as evidence within this trial. I object to Mr. Niemann using evidence in this way to advise the Court upon matters that this witness may have been told by other people which may or may not be true.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So your objection is that it is hearsay, not probative?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Mr. Niemann, would you rephrase your question or repeat the question? Was your question, did you hear someone called Tadic at Omarska? Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Your objection will be overruled, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I then went on to say, tell us the circumstances under which you heard that name. (To the witness): Could you tell us the circumstances under which you heard the name "Tadic" mentioned when you were in the camp at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While they were beating us, I heard the name "Tadic" mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is the answer. The answer he heard his name mentioned, not what was said about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If this is to be the substance of the answer, in view of my earlier cross-examination which the Court is aware of, "they were using the name 'Tadic' whilst they were beating us in Omarska", I expect the Court will give such weight to it as it thinks appropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Our discussion, though, related to a different item. Our discussion related to the meaning of Mr. Niemann's question. The meaning of his question, not the meaning but the actual phrasing of the question has been made clear. We consider that it is not objectionable and your objection will be overruled. Your question now was whether or not he heard the name Tadic mentioned in Omarska. The answer was, yes. You then asked the witness what were the circumstances surrounding his hearing the name Tadic mentioned. Now he is going to tell us the circumstances; was he being beaten at the time, was he asleep, was he awake, was he in the white house, where was he?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, please, Mr. Halvadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was all -- my head was broken in several places. I was all black, because I had been beaten every day, and I heard all sorts of names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the precise circumstances when you heard the name Tadic mentioned when you were in Omarska camp? Can you tell us approximately when it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to sit down. We had to sit on the floor. It was a small room in the white house first to the right-hand side, or on the left, sorry, as you come into the white house. It was a small room, two by three metres, about 12 square metres, and there were always 13 people there. We had to sit face down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear this name mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the person that used the name Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not allowed to look anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the person that, apparently, had the name Tadic when you were in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was happening at the time when you heard this name Tadic mentioned in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They started kicking me and I fainted again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No re-examination, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have just one question of the witness. Sir, you testified that, "I would seek out war criminals myself". It is not clear to me whether that was a statement or whether it was a question. This was during the time that Mr. Key was questioning you on cross-examination. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: War criminals should all be punished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that, "I would seek out war criminals myself". What do you mean by that? Had you been seeking out war criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not but I had intended at one time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To do what, to seek out war criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you seek them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How would I seek them out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you intend to seek them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I had found any, I would have killed them on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the time that you were with the armed resistance group in the former Yugoslavia or are you referring to some later time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some later time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What later time was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was in [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this a matter that needs redaction although we have touched on this a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I heard it twice so far mentioned and I thought on those two occasions ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why do not we just -- if you wish to have it redacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Is there any objection? We can look at the time. Is there any objection to this reference being redacted as well as the two previous ones which were not as obvious?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Has it been resolved, Miss Featherstone?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we have them, 15.14.42, 15.02.42 and 14.54.08.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Continuing with the questions that I have been asking of the witness regarding his involvement in seeking out war criminals, I will either continue with those questions or, if you wish, Mr. Kay, you may continue with that line of questioning if you wish -- you tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not concerned to follow the matters any further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I am. Maybe you have statements, you two have statements you know, but I am interested and it may relate to how I view the testimony of the witness. When was this -- again now, Mr. Niemann, you will have to help me because if this is the subject of a redaction maybe I should not proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour. If your Honour could just warn the witness not to mention places?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. (To the witness): As I ask you these questions, sir, do not mention places when you respond to my questions, if you can. You testified that subsequently then you became interested in seeking out war criminals. Would you explain to me, was that a part of a group, when did you become a part of that group and what you have done in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have that in mind, but this is the fury that was created and when I remember all that happened to me, I just get angry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you sought out any war criminals? You said you intended to but have you actually sought out any war criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. You may be excused, sir. Is there any objection to the witness being permanently excused, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Halvadzic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution called Mr. Kasim Mesic to the stand. MR. KASIM MESIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take that oath that is being given to you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. KEEGAN

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Your full name is Kasim Mesic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your date of birth is 21st March 1944?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in the town of Cela in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you raised in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have four years of primary school education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you subsequently trained as a mason and work at that profession for seven years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you serve your compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long of a period was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18 months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you trained to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a sergeant, I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you trained in the infantry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your compulsory service did you return to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do any reserve military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was once in reserve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the year after you returned, 1966?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever serve in the TO unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Raskovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you returned from your compulsory military service did you work as a mason again for a time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that did you work in a factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a paper factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 where were you working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was working in the Mira Cikota Company in Prijedor in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Did you unload trucks at that factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was involved in transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stop working in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you have to stop working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Muslims were banned, were not allowed to work -- because Muslims were banned from work. They were not allowed to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, when you are giving your answer if you could speak up just a little bit, please? Who told you that Muslims were banned and not allowed to work any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Manager, Topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What nationality was the Manager, Topic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few days after you were told you were no longer allowed to work, did you witness the shelling of the Hambarine area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you remember first about the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember them announcing that Mirza Mujadzic must surrender, and then if he did not surrender that they will shell Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that yourself on the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Neighbours heard it on the radio. I did not have a radio and they said that, unless Mirza Mujadzic surrendered by 2 o'clock, they would shell Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when the shelling did start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was about 2.00, half past 2, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when that shelling started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got ready. My wife and my son, I sent them to the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that to your cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, a neighbour of mine, Jusa Adzim and Cedo Balaban, and there were two cellars there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, they need you to speak closer to the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not go to the cellars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did not go to the cellar because I was also all astounded, completely bewildered, when the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you, in fact, do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started towards the Sana, and I looked at people and they were running from above, down towards the woods, towards the forest, next to the Sana; and then I remembered, what am I going to do there? I mean, there is shelling all over. So I turned and went back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went out of your house towards the Sana River?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From there could you, in fact, look over to the Hambarine area and see the shells hitting buildings there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of buildings were in that area that were being shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were homes, private houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see people running from those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were closer to the Sana and were fleeing towards that forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that you could see running in the direction of the forest and the Sana River, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No-one in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No-one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell where the shells were coming from, where they were being fired from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Topica, Brdo, Pasinac, Karan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you tell that the shells were being fired from those positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, smoke could be seen. The smoke was coming upwards, rising up, and whenever it came up it meant that a shell had hit Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Are you talking you could see the smoke when the shells landed in Hambarine or you could see the smoke from the guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they were fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have Exhibit 79 which is a map already admitted of the Prijedor area placed on the elmo, please? Could we have the elmo turned on, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have Exhibit 79 with me. We can share it, if you wish, Mr. Keegan, if it is not coming on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. This is the actual 79. Just for clarification for the Court, the stickers are to indicate those areas he just mentioned. That is all. (To the witness): Mr. Mesic, you have seen this map before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The area marked with the "A", that is the area of Raskovac in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the area that is between the railroad and the Sana River, by the area which ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the letter "A" appears. The letter "B" marks the area of Hambarine from where you could see the shells impacting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The letter "C" is generally the area of Karan which you mentioned earlier, one position from which the shells were being fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The letter "D" is Pasinac in the vicinity of the ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- airports and the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Barracks, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "E" is the Topic Brdo area at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mesic, as the shelling of Hambarine was ending was there also some activity in your neighbourhood, the Raskovac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, police came to collect weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were asking for them. They were asking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the people in your neighbourhood turn weapons over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but they did not have them, only two had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two pistols. That was all there was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that day did forces come to your neighbourhood who referred to themselves as the police who arrested people who lived in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came down there by the road somewhere, passing, going down the streets and arresting and taking away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see those people who arrested people in your neighbourhood on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We looked down towards the road as they were taking those people and then a friend of ours, a Serb dressed as a soldier, he stopped there and then he came to us and told us, "Hide some place", and we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that Serb who told you to hide, he was your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you hesitant to reveal his identity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you arrested on that day with the other people in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I hid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the people look like, the forces who came to arrest the people in your neighbourhood that day, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some of them were in multi-coloured uniforms, in military uniforms. They had some red berets and they ran and walked and so ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "military uniforms", what type of military uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, listen, there were all sorts of them. There were really all kinds of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there also uniforms referred to as SMB, the old JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those people have any particular insignia on their uniforms that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that, properly speaking. Some did have some Kokards. Some had something, I do not know how to put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some have some ribbons on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour were those ribbons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were the colours of the Yugoslav flag. They were tied round here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: White, red and blue were the colours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were tied around the epaulets on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who any of those forces were that day, did you recognise any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not anyone; we did not dare look. We were running away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you subsequently arrested yourself on another day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was some four or five days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the circumstances of that arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A group turned up, a group of men, of soldiers, those policemen. They were shouting saying they were policemen. There were about 10 of them in a van, and they caught us and next to my house, myself, my son, 16 year old, and there were three nephews of mine were there. We were sitting and talking and that is how they surrounded us and got us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men who identified themselves or called themselves police, how were they dressed, what type of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were in multi-coloured uniforms, some had black ribbons, black head bands around their head and only one had a black beret on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "multi-coloured uniforms" are you referring to camouflage uniforms or different types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, mottled, they were many coloured, they wore those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those men have any insignia on their uniform that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some had with four S’s and others I saw nothing. Perhaps those Kokard, yes, some had Kokard, some did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the four S’s, are you referring to the symbol which is a cross with the four Cyrillic Ss which look like the Latin C in the corners of the crosses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those men rounded up yourself and the other men in the area, what did they do with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They forced us to stand against the house, to raise three fingers like this and against a wall, and then they came behind our back and beat us and then they brought another three neighbours, three brothers, and one of them was also a minor, and two more neighbours and my two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the record reflect that the witness held out his hands at approximately head level out from his shoulders with the thumb and first two fingers of each hand extended?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Is that the way you had to keep your hands against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with the legs spread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men in all were rounded up and placed against that wall on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about a dozen of them came, others went to neighbours and four or five, I think, stayed there with us to beat us next to our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, how many men in all were rounded up by the police and forced to stand against that wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 11 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background of all of those men who were lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were beaten while you were forced to stand against the wall. Can you describe how you and the other men were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They moved from one to the other, three times with a baton at the back of the neck, then kicking with their boots in the stomach with rifle butts and then between the legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "between the legs", were you kicked in your genitals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they hit you with the rifle butts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the back, on the back, he hit me on the left side and injured four ribs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you hit in the area of the kidneys?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you suffer any injuries as a result of these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was bruised -- we were all bruised and, well, there was some blood on our heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel any effect from being hit in the ribs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it hurt and I took an X-ray in [redacted] and when I arrived in [redacted] there was still blood coagulated because we did not have doctors back there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have problems breathing immediately after that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you wish a redaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. 15.44.28. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Keegan. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. It will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long did these beatings go on for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For about an hour, hour and a half, two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They loaded us all on to a van and took us to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the "SUP", you refer to the police station in the centre of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the SUP where were you taken first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to the house facilities, detention facilities they had there in the yard. They had these cells and they were standing in a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that took you to the cell in the police station of Prijedor? Was it the men ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those who had brought us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody already in the cell when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the roof, yes, but in the cell, they brought us into the cell beating us all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there someone already in the cell when you got there, another prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody beat us. No, nobody beat us until we came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, when were you put into the cell, was there already another prisoner in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a Croat there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that he was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how could I not know? I mean, he said. I mean, I know. He said he was a Croat. He was covered in blood too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the cell where were you all taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then from the cell they took us out, again put us against a wall and we raised three fingers again and spread our arms and our legs, and they took our boot laces and our belts and our wallets, everything of value that we had. They all took that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They took all your valuables. What did they do with your documents and identification papers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They threw them away on the ground, on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you all beaten there in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us again. The police came to beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those individuals which you just said were police, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the normal police uniform, a light blue shirt with dark blue trousers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, light blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you beaten by those police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us with their hands, with palms of their hands, and all sorts of things, but mostly with their open palms of their hands, the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did these beatings go on for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it also lasted for about two hours there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you and the other individuals who were beaten looked like after these beatings were over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother lost consciousness because he was hit here and he lost two teeth there and his face was injured and were totally impotent. We had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that the witness pointed to his right cheek.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will so reflect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Where were you taken from the police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The vehicle, it looked like a car but it was a van, and there were only two benches there so six people could fit in, and they, nevertheless, loaded all 12 of us on to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was the eleven people who had been rounded up in your neighbourhood plus the Croat who was already at the police station when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the van did they make you do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We sang "Who says who lies Serbia is small".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the camp what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they got us off the van and we again had to be against a wall, again with three fingers against a wall, and those two who had brought us and other guards who were there. Then they put us into a garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two who brought you to the camp, were they from the group who had rounded you up in your neighbourhood or were they police from the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know where they come from or what they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they dressed in the multi-coloured uniforms or were they dressed in the normal police uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those of many colours uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they put you against the wall when you arrived at the camp, were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They kicked us with their feet, with all sorts of things, with batons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you kicked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the back and between the legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again when you say "between the legs" do you mean you were kicked in the genitals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the back were they concentrating in a particular area of your back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where? Were they concentrating on your lower back or upper back or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All over. We were in all colours like a snake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In all colours like a snake", do you mean from the bruising?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they curse at you while they were beating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did, "May Alija fuck your mother. You have come here because of Alija" and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they said "you came here because of Alija", who were they referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The President of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you forced to sing any songs when you arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What song?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they told us to sing something about Karadjordje and we did not know any so we sang again "Who says who lies".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Who says who lies Serbia is small"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were then put in a garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the garage that is in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were put into that garage were there already prisoners in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were many prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those prisoners do anything for you when you were placed in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they got their shirts off and tried to cover them, cover the bruises where we were bruised on our backs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they place water on the shirts first before they put them on your backs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the other prisoners that were in that garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in Omarska, what was the ethnic group of most of the guards that you came into contact with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs. The Orthodox Serbs. They had become Serbs overnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days were you held in that small garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 to 25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in that garage, were prisoners called out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, later on they started calling out people and taking them for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the first couple of days how were people taken out of that garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening they would come and take out one or two, only point with a finger who is to come out, and he comes out and would never return to the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of those people who were taken out at night anywhere else in the camp while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the people were called out for interrogation, how would they be called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would bring a list with them and then call out names from that list for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear in this small garage what was going on in the interrogation rooms upstairs in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of us screaming upstairs while they were being interrogating, those people above us, above the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually called out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 20, 25 days they called me for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten on the way to your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did that beating take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the access to the staircase, up the stairs and to the room through the corridor, they were standing in a line there and beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they were standing in a line", who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guards in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were standing by the stairs, below the staircase below and upstairs at the end of the staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were taken upstairs, which room were you taken into for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up the stairs in the first room to the right -- to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First room to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the person who was interrogating you have a uniform on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of many colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked me where was my rifle, that was straightaway, and I said I did not have a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ask any questions other than about weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nothing else, only about the weapons. So, writing down something in a book. I do not know what he was writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of the interrogation were you asked to sign something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that sheet I had to sign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take time to read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not dare read it. I only signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were taken out of the interrogation room were you beaten on the way out of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, down to the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you came out of the building you were placed on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that would be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before we recess, for the record, Prosecution Exhibit 242 has 13 photos in it. They are numbered beginning with the first one, it is No. 00400134, and the second one is numbered 00400135, it is also numbered 00400136, and the remaining photos are numbered consecutively. I do not know what your copy shows, Mr. Wladimiroff, but that is what is in evidence. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (4.20 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, before I start my questioning again, just for the record, when we broke you mentioned the prior Exhibit 242 and the numbers which were on the back of photograph No. 2 in particular. Just for the record, your Honour (and the Defence is aware of this) those numbers are the evidence record numbers, which are stamped on the photograph after it is brought back by the investigators from the witness and it is logged into our system. There are two on the photograph which the witness signs because the photograph is copied; one number relates to the front of the photograph, the picture, the second number relates to the signature.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I see. I did not know the reason for the two photos, but I do recall that the witness said that those numbers were not on there when he identified -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Correct, so in each of the books you will note that every picture is numbered and one, you would normally have two; anyone that signs should normally have two ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: -- for that reason.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was the only one that was signed in the group. Good. Thank you. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Mr. Mesic, when we broke for the recess you were just describing how you were brought to the pista after your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the pista did you see anyone whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw my nephew, and he called me to sit down next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were on the pista for that day did you witness a shooting of a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The young man was killed. He went to ask for bread, because he was giving out bread to minors and he went to have some bread. The guard pushed him away. They did not give him any bread. He walked between us, among us. He shouted a little bit and then a guard came, put him aside and sent him to the white house. He came at the door, at the bottom door, he went into the room. The window was open. Under that window there was a bench and he jumped out the window and sat on the bench and a little while after that he jumped, he raised his hands and said, "I have power", and he started walking towards the policeman. The guard took a rifle and fired an entire round of bullets into his lower part and he fell down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the prisoner fell down, did the guards -- well, what did you see next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went, a soldier went in a camouflage uniform, he came up to him, close to him, and the other people said, "Here is Tadic". I turned around to see who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, I have an objection here again on the principle that the evidence just adduced through the witness, its probative value is substantially outweighed by its prejudice on the basis that it is speech by other people informing this witness of the identity of a person. Those people who give that information are not witnesses that we have been made aware of, nor witnesses that we can question or challenge. We do not know how right or wrong and on what basis they received the information themselves, whether they knew the man or not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
