utterances.text: That is really the subject of your cross-examination or at some point when you wish to question this witness, and that is the circumstances surrounding his gathering of this information or hearing "Here is Tadic". I will overrule your objection at this time again -- well, we have not ruled on your submission, but it seems appropriate, at least at this point, to hear the testimony before we can really gauge what its probative value is because I do not know the circumstances surrounding it. At this point, other than there was a shooting in the lower part of an individual, the guard discharging a round and somebody says, "Here is Tadic", that is all we know at this point. So I will overrule your objection at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, you indicated that a soldier dressed in camouflage uniform, you said, walked up to him. Do you mean a soldier in a camouflage uniform walked up to the guard who had shot the prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that person dressed in a camouflage uniform was walking up to the guard who had shot the prisoner, did fellow prisoners say something to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone identify the soldier who was walking up to the guard who had shot the prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The prisoner said, "That was Tadic" and I looked at him and then I turned away, and then he said, "Hello" to that guard and they smiled at each other. He was carrying a book. I do not know whether it was a novel or a notebook to write down about the murder. I do not know what that object was, but at that moment there was a command for us to sit down, to lie down with our face facing the earth. We lay down, facing down. After that there was a command for us to get up, and then Kera was put in a blanket and was taken behind the garage, and he was put there behind the room where he was and the others started washing the blood away from the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, when that soldier in the camouflage uniform walked up to the guard, did one prisoner mention the name "Tadic" or was there more than one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More than one, "Here, here is Tadic coming again".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall those people saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said it was Tadic, and they are competing with each other as to who will kill more people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The prisoners around you that mentioned, who said, "Here is Tadic coming again", do you know where those prisoners were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were from all places around the area. My nephew was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The prisoners whom you heard say, "Here is Tadic", do you know where those particular prisoners were from, what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were mostly from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get a good look at the face of the man who they identified as Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said after you saw that man you looked away. You then described how the man greeted the guard who had shot the prisoner. Does that mean you looked again over at the area where the guard and this man identified as Tadic were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do when this man who was identified as Tadic came up to the guard? How did they greet each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They shook hands and smiled at each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that about that same time an order was given for everyone to lay down and not to look. When you did that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we lay down facing down. Someone was sitting, some people were sitting and looking down, and then you could look under your arm what was going on around you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked up again, could you see Tadic any more, the man identified as Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the command came for us to stand up, I could no longer see Tadic, if it was Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from the pista that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day I was on the pista until about 9 or 10 o'clock and then we were thrown into room No. 16, who wanted to go, and I was among those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you join the group that was going into a room in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because upstairs it was all closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You thought it would be better conditions if you were inside the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I thought it would be better -- I would have better conditions and we would not be abused as much in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to the body of the prisoner named Kera who was shot that afternoon you were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That body remained there until the following morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because in the morning we went to the meadow, to the toilet. We were driven out there and there we saw when the bodies were loaded. There were several other bodies and Kera's body was among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you were driven out there, do you mean the guards took you from the room inside the hangar outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the area that you were supposed to use as a toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see the body of Kera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the same place where it was left, behind the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see them do with the bodies that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were putting them on a small lorry and driving them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the man who had been identified to you as Tadic in the camp again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the morning we left when we spent the night and when we went out to go to the toilet and went back, I was sitting next to that man. He said he was from Kozarac, and then a guard came and told me that I had to take him for interrogation upstairs, that he should follow me. We went upstairs. I took him up the stairs. We were beaten a little bit on the way up. He went to the right, in the third room to the right. I was left to face the wall and raise three fingers and I was standing like that until he came out. I saw Tadic there at a desk and there were also chairs around the table. He lifted his feet on the table and when I saw him I said to myself, this is the same man I saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were taken to the field for the toilet in the morning, you were taken back upstairs into the same room in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that room there was a man -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not taken back. I was taken back. He remained on the pista, the man from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to before you went to the interrogation with him. So were you taken back to room 16 that morning and a man from Kozarac was brought into room 16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were told by a guard to take that man to interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because he was really beaten up and he could not walk on his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took that man to the upstairs in the administration building where the interrogations were conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is there that you saw the man identified as Tadic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had brought the man from Kozarac to the interrogation room where did you stand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the corridor about two metres from him, from Tadic, that man, I do not know if it was Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you told to stand again the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to raise three fingers and stand against the wall until he came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long do you think you were in that hallway waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not very long -- about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time did you get a good look at the man who was identified to you as Tadic who was sitting at the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could, with the assistance of Miss Sutherland, I would like you to point out on the model the various locations that we have discussed. If you could stand up, please, Mr. Mesic? Mr. Mesic, if you stand over next to your desk, to the witness desk?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you wish, Mr. Keegan, he can come around this side and use these microphones. I do not know where you want him to identify. Do as you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I think he can probably reach all the sides better from there, Ma'am. In addition, they do not have the long headphones available, unfortunately. I looked but they are not there today. Mr. Mesic, if you could, could you please point first to the small garage where you were held when you first arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model) This is the garage, this. This is the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, your Honour, I think at least the Court is familiar enough with the model to appreciate that it is the small garage located in the ground floor in the corner of that building. There we are. If you could point again to that garage, please? Thank you. If you could point now to the interrogation room in the administration building where you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interrogated in this room upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a letter and number in there identifying that room, if you could read that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is No. 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken out to the pista and you saw the shooting of Kera, where were you approximately on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was next to the flower pots near the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flower pots that were closest to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was close there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, if you could now point to the room where you were taken in the hangar that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the hangar?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Where you were taken in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point again and then identify it by a letter or number that is inside that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand your question quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point again to the room in the hangar where you stayed, in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness's answer was not interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The room where you were taken after you were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could identify that by the number or letter that is inside that model?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could indicate the room in that white house where Kera was taken before he was shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was taken through the door and was put into this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the first room on the left as you look at the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a bench outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The window that is indicated on the model there in the front, that is the window that he jumped out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, though the window was opened, he jumped up and sat down on the bench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were in room 16, were you ever taken to another room in that hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in that room was there a significant event which occurred when more prisoners were brought in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought three bus loads of people from Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do with you and the other prisoners who were already in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They transferred us along the corridor, along the hall, to another room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point to that other room, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Along the corridor from this room to this other room. That room over there. We came out of here, and went directly to that door. There was a staircase here, Cigo came there. He placed a guard, our door was open, with a rifle, told him how to hold the rifle and then placed us there. We were in this room here, and then they started beating the people from Hambarine and then brought them to our room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, could you point again to the room where you were placed when the men from Hambarine were brought, just point again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see quite, but this is the room, yes. This is the room where we were before, and then from this room, when the people from Hambarine came, they transferred us to this room here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can resume your seat now? For the record, your Honour, because of the limitations of the witness being able to reach it, it was room B7 that the witness was pointing to.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That he was transferred?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Transferred to, correct, your Honour. (To the witness): When those men from Hambarine were brought into the room you have identified as room 16, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were those men beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat them during interrogation and they beat them until 9 o'clock in the evening, until half past 8 or 9.00, I am not quite sure, and then they threw them into, the two to No. 16 and they asked us who would like to go over to the other room. Some of us transferred back to our room again. The people were beaten up. I asked one of them where they were from and he said, "We were from Hambarine; they caught us in the woods and brought us here".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the room, room 16, look like when you went back in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was blood. There was all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those men stay in that room all night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, about 11, half past 11 in the evening, they called them out and put them on a bus. The buses were standing by the pista. There were three of them I saw exactly through a hole in the window. Then they called them out, while beating them and forcing them to go on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on that night did you hear anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a shooting from a distance that night. That is when they took my brother away and three of his sons and a brother of a son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the shooting in the camp itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, a little bit at a distance. It was a sort of strange sort of sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much shooting was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was for about 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave Omarska camp, Mr. Mesic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when the whole thing fell apart, I do not know the exact date. We were simply loaded on to buses and took us to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the trip to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could even reach Australia to which we arrived by the time we arrived in Manjaca. They were beating us and they loaded us on to buses like cattle. We were sitting along corridors. I sat on the stairs. There were other people sitting next to me, and then around half past 4, I am not quite sure, or perhaps 5 o'clock, and we set off for Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they beat people on the buses during that trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trampled on us, stepped on us, they ill-treated us, singing and beating. Everything went on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have the heat on in the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they give you any water or any food while you were on the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I have a discharge list and I have this card of the Geneva Convention with which we registered us. That is how I remember it and I celebrate it as my birthday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken when you left Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Manjaca, we were taken to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you were transferred from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They transferred from Manjaca those who were elderly, who were sick, and minors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of condition were you in when you were transferred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I think they were quite good at Manjaca, the conditions, because it appeared that they were planning to kill all the inmates, those from Omarska, the guards and Joja, I do not know what his first name or his family name is, but I know he comes from Omarska and they called him Joja. He was the one who worst ill-treated us, who beat us and then the Deputy Camp Commander came. He came there and he threw abuses at them, said, "Why did you not do it there in Prijedor, in Omarska? You are not going to do anything here" and that is how he saved us. When we got off, he gave us water and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about the Deputy Camp Commander at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What condition were you in, physical condition were you in, when you were transferred from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very bad. I did not think I would get back home alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you walk at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much did you weigh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thirty-eight kilogrammes it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then a neighbour Vlado Tubin came with my brother's horses and his cart and he came to fetch us. Kuruzovic managed to release me and that is how he took us back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the man identified to you as Tadic again in Bosnia-Herzegovina once you left the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, have you ever seen a picture of the man who was identified to you as Tadic on TV or in any newspaper or in any magazine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June of this year were you shown a book of photographs by an investigator from the tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the number of that book? Did it have the number on the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this book marked as the next exhibit in order, please, it will be number 243, and then handed to the witness. Mr. Mesic, if you would take a look at that book. Do you recognise that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the book itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which book?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The book of all the pictures you are looking at, do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the book you were shown by the investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the investigator showed you that book, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To sign the photograph on this album of photographs and I took the picture, the photograph, and I signed it to recognise it, that person who was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. When he first handed you the book what did he tell you to do when he very first handed you the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, whether I recognised here in the book who was that Tadic whom I recognised, because I had never seen that Tadic until that time. I had never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he handed you the book did he tell you to look for the man Tadic? Is that what he told you to do? Did he use that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. No, only "Do you recognise, do you recognise that picture and which you thought was Tadic?" I do not remember exactly. No, he asked me to recognise among, to try to identify him among all those men who was that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look at each picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you select any picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, the fourth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign the back of that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the picture that you selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they told me it was Tadic, so I signed that it was Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that the man whose picture that you chose in that book is the man who was identified to you as Tadic in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was, is there any doubt in your mind that that is the man whom you saw in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that man there and the picture and they are the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you the question, who was the picture that you selected, the answer which was translated was, "Well, they told me it was Tadic, so I signed that it was Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that that man was Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I recognised him. I recognised the picture of the man, but whether he is Tadic or not ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say "they" you are referring to the people in the camp who said, "Here comes Tadic" on the day you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not referring to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour. I am sorry, I would tender Exhibit 243, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection to 243? You have a running objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be overruled at this time. Exhibit 243 will be admitted. Mr. Kay, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesic, you were only on the pista for one day, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day you were on the pista, are you able to tell the Court how many other people were on the pista with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I really was not in a state to count people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of state were you in on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beaten one might say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have cuts? Were you bleeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the face, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your body painful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it that you got on to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came around 5 or 6 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us anything about the date as to when it was that you got on to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us for how long you had been in Omarska by the time you came on to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even that I would not know exactly, when I was brought there or how long I was. A man cannot remember everything. I still do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pista, is it right that it was bounded by flower tubs or boxes, concrete boxes on each end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who were in that area of the pista, was it a large number of people? Was the area full?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many hundreds of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hundreds? Well, I think -- no, I do not know. I do not know exactly how many, but the pista was full. People spent the night lying down around the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the other building did you walk out of the doors at the front of the building on to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The doors that we see in the model in the court, perhaps you can see it from where you are there, if you would like to stand up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From interrogation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could indicate to us where you entered the pista from? Perhaps if you stand up ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model) 21, that is it, that is where we came out and came here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pointer that you used there indicated that you were over towards the grass, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flower tubs, are you able to indicate where they were by standing up and showing us with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the flower tubs, well, you know it, I mean they were on one side and on the other side. I did not really draw it where they were exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could stand up and indicate to us with the use of the pointer where the flower tubs were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The flower tubs were like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between this and they went in that direction. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men on the pista, were they between the flower tubs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were all sitting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flower tubs was the boundary of the area where the men were held who were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know that, whether they drew a boundary, put a boundary somewhere or whether they considered it a boundary. I would not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were between the flower beds, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would indicate that your mark that you gave the Court that you were nearer the grass where the white house is was in fact wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huh! How could it not be true when I sat next to the flower tubs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flower tubs were between the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could they?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you just indicated them to us not a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Listen, I cannot describe it now, no way. I am simply not up to it. Where was what, how do I know now? It is all ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you these questions ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sitting next to the flower tubs next to the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you these questions as you apparently can remember what the man looked like who you say was Tadic from those photographs, and you say you can identify him from those photographs as the man you saw who spoke to the guard who shot Kere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, are you telling us that your memory about that is good and your memory about other things is good? Or are you saying your memory is poor about the other things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do I know where the flower tubs are and the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I am asking you these things and, if you can remember, please tell us. Now, did you know the man Kere at all? Was he a relative or a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was my fellow worker. We worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was he a friend or not a friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was on a different transport. We were not friends. He is not the same age. We could not be friends because we were of a different age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Kere asked the guard for bread where was the guard? Can you stand ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the door, in front of the canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the door that you indicated to us some 10 minutes ago that you entered, that you left to enter the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the man Kere asked for bread. How did he come to end up at the white house entering on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard called him and took him into the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which guard called him and took him into the white house? Where was that guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was there with the one who was distributing bread and Kere got angry and started shouting. He told him he would take him into the white house and he took him into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the guard moved with Kere across the pista and put him in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guard remain there or leave that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came back. He came back and the other one was standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did he join the other guard who was in front of the canteen building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the guard that took Kere over to the white house, did he leave him there and go back to the canteen building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and one was standing there and one stood by the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Kere jumped out of the window and sat on a bench in front of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, that is correct, and then he stood up, started towards the guard, towards us, and raised his arms like this and said, "I have power", and he snatched his rifle immediately and shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that guard who shot him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Close to us, to the flower tubs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guard shoot over the head of the prisoners on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because he fired in the direction of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the guard fired his rifle at that man, what did the prisoners on the pista do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lie down, straightaway, but when he moved, that soldier when he came, went to him and when they greeted each other that is when the orders came that we should lie down on our stomachs and keep our heads down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when the firing happened everyone went to protect themselves by lying down so that they came to no harm, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were watching. When that gentleman came, when a guard came to another guard, they greeted each other and that is when the orders came for us to lie down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you lie down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sitting and with my head bowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until that moment had you been watching the guard who shot Kere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the thing that most interested you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had never seen a man die like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know the prisoners you were amongst on the pista were from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were from all over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us of your nephew whom you joined. Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Raskovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how could he be from Kozarac? He was from Raskovac. They were all from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were all from there, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Listen, sir, you are slightly exceeding the limit. Does it mean if I am from Raskovac everybody is from Raskovac and if I am from Kozarac and then everybody is from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know whether the Court wants to adjourn at this stage. There is more questioning and the witness has been in the box for some time. Maybe it is an opportunity for a break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, we should adjourn at 5.30. It is one minute to 5.30. The last Exhibit was 243, is it? The last photo book?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Has that been sufficiently identified for everyone, the numbers of photos in there, the numbers that are on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I will have another glance.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Pass it to me. I guess I am the only one who is overly concerned that one of those photos will fall out and then there will be a disagreement about what was in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Maybe, your Honour, it would be a good idea to have copies of each book because the sequence may differ. Therefore, we rather prefer to see the sequence too.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor should make a copy of the actual book that he intends, that it intends to offer for you, is that not what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is an excellent idea. You have given them an opportunity to look at it, but the actual exhibit why don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, and the point of having those numbers stamped on the back is when it comes in it is logged with exactly the number of the pictures so you can tell exactly which pictures were in that book by number. So that is one way of safeguarding that issue, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am just concerned that Mr. Bos is going to be holding on to 243 -- I do not know how many photos are in 243 and I do not know which numbers they are, and I can see that the pages at the top are not stapled. I am concerned something might fall out, that is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There are copies already in the evidence system and those that can be provided. That is what I am indicating.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I want the Defence to know and receive an exact copy of what is Exhibit 243. You will do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Then we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. Thank you. (5.30 p.m.)

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned until the following day)
